Commit 3d19382 touched only invariant-guard.sh and hook-wiring-parity.bats. Here it is left standing in the more authoritative artifact — the one SC-4 names by hand and the one future changes reason from.
issues.fix: One sentence in docs/INVARIANTS.md:472, matched to the guard comment's wording.

issues.title: INV-13's statement of its only exemption is now false in the no-baseline branch
issues.detail: INV-13 states: 면제되는 것은 애초에 훅을 배선하지 않는 settings 파일(예: enabledPlugins만 담은 것)뿐이다 — OLD 집합이 공집합이라 통과한다. Measured: a settings.json that never wired any hook is exempt while parseable (exit 0) but is DENIED once the disk copy is unparseable with no HEAD baseline (exit 2), because the exemption is computed from OLD_R and the none branch never reaches it. Pre-F76 the same input was exit 0.
issues.measured: parseable + del(.hooks) + enable disableAllHooks -> exit 0; unparseable + del(.hooks) + same edit -> exit 2; pre-F76 guard on the same unparseable input -> exit 0.
issues.why_it_matters: This is a SECOND accepted cost of the no-baseline branch and it is documented nowhere — neither in the code comment (which names only the restore-an-enabled-switch cost) nor in INV-13. The direction is fail-closed, so it is over-blocking rather than a hole, but the round-2 theme of this feature is precisely 'state the cost accurately'.
issues.fix: Add the second cost to the same paragraph that states the first, and scope the exemption sentence to the parseable branch.

issues.title: The hooks.json branch's guard_registered() axis still reads raw disk, not the baseline — the same class F76 claims to have closed
issues.detail: invariant-guard.sh:967 still calls guard_registered "$(cat "$FILE")". On an unparseable disk that call silently evaluates false and the INV-7 self-protection check disappears — exactly the 'parse failure turns a check off' shape F76 exists to close. Its siblings in the same branch (OLD_R / MISSING) were made baseline-aware; this one was not.
issues.measured: hooks.json registering invariant-guard.sh OUTSIDE the .hooks structure (so wired_rows misses it and only guard_registered defends it): disk parseable, removal -> exit 2; disk unparseable WITH a valid HEAD baseline, same removal -> exit 0. Pre-F76 also exit 0, so this is pre-existing, not a regression.
issues.why_it_matters: Narrow exposure (needs a registration outside .hooks, which is unusual), and out of the contract's literal scope. But it is a measured counter-example to the commit's and INV-13's framing that the class — not just the instance — was closed across both wiring files.
issues.fix: Feed $__baseline to guard_registered instead of cat "$FILE", or record the axis as a known residual in INV-13.

issues.title: The round-2 commit message credits itself with a test change it did not make, and overstates an assertion
issues.detail: The message says: 'AC-6 named three kill switches; the cases now iterate all three in both branches and assert the deny reason names the switch that fired.' Measured against the diff: 3d19382 changed only the f76_guard orig_jq plumbing and the one cost-test call site. The three-switch iteration was already present in the parent 3f48f6c (added by round-1 follow-up 261758d). Furthermore the deny-reason assertion exists ONLY in the head-baseline test; the no-baseline test asserts exit status alone — so 'in both branches' is false.
issues.why_it_matters: Same class as I-1: a new unmeasured claim made inside the commit whose purpose is to retract unmeasured claims. No behavioural impact — mutation M5 confirms the no-baseline test does catch switch-list narrowing even without the message assertion.
issues.fix: Correct the commit message in any follow-up, or add the deny-reason assertion to the no-baseline case so the sentence becomes true.

issues.title: The F76 head-baseline fixture silently degrades to the no-baseline branch when CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is exported
issues.detail: __head_content_for prefers CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR over git rev-parse. f76_guard builds its fixture repo in mktemp -d, outside any CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. Measured: with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR unset, AC-1's wiring removal -> exit 2; with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR set to the repo root, the identical input -> exit 0, because the file no longer resolves under the derived root and baseline_kind falls back to none.
issues.why_it_matters: The suite's result depends on an ambient environment variable that IS set in a normal Claude Code session (it is set in this session's MCP sandbox, unset in the Bash tool shell — which is why my run of bats went green). It fails loudly rather than silently, so it is a false-failure risk, not a false pass. It also means INV-13's branch table overstates the head-baseline branch's reach: it applies only to wiring files that resolve under the derived root, not to every file present in HEAD.
issues.fix: Have f76_guard export CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$d" (or unset it) so the branch under test is pinned rather than inherited.

issues.title: The delete-then-recreate defense is skipped WITHOUT any warning when the edited file lies outside CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR
issues.detail: The 'root 해석 실패' warning fires only when __root is empty. When CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is set but the target file is not under it, __head_content_for returns early with __head_root empty and __head_root_failed=0 — the defense does not apply and nothing is printed. Measured identically on pre-F76 and HEAD guards (both exit 0), so this is pre-existing and NOT an F76 regression.
issues.why_it_matters: Same 'silent no-op' family F76 is about; worth a backlog line since the refactor put this logic in a shared function where the fix would now be one place instead of two.

verified_claims.claim: '부모 커밋이라고 쓰면 거짓이다: 직전 커밋은 이미 이 동작을 담고 있어 실측 exit 2 다' (J-2 correction)

TRUE. bats tests/ run with no pipe: '1..793', 793 ok, 0 not ok, BATS_EXIT=0.

mutation_matrix._note: My own seven mutations, injected into a git-archive mirror of HEAD (the repo working tree was never modified — verified clean before and after). Each injection was verified to have actually applied (md5 + bash -n) before its result was read; two early perl attempts silently no-opped and were discarded rather than reported, which is the same verification failure the commit message describes.
mutation_matrix.conclusion: Every mutation is caught, each by the test that should catch it. The accepted-cost test is killed by three distinct mutations and by nothing else — it is both sensitive and specific. J-1's defect is genuinely fixed.

No criterion pins the environment the head-baseline branch is exercised in (I-5); the branch under test is inherited from the ambient CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR rather than fixed by the fixture.
ambiguous_criteria: SC-4 says '이 수정으로 참이 되거나 거짓이 되는 문장을 역방향으로 점검' but names only the F75 '(2) 단순화' paragraph as the concrete target. The named item WAS handled; the unnamed ones (I-1, I-2) were not. A criterion that names one instance invites closing that instance — the same instance-vs-class failure INV-13 documents. Future contracts should require enumerating every INV-N sentence touched, not just the flagged one.
